title: The same in-page push bid.ext bid under the plain IAB dialect draws payload_missing

source.name: ortbtools In-Page Push dialect contract — dialect-selection contrast (default IAB dialect vs inpage-push)
source.notes: Same bid.ext bytes as the canonical-field sibling case, analyzed under case.dialect 'iab' instead of 'inpage-push', to demonstrate the documented contract difference: only the In-Page Push dialect exposes claimsBid() to suppress the base IAB payload_missing check.

modifications: Wholly original OpenRTB envelope, imp, site, device and bid fields; bid.ext values are the same canonical set used in the sibling case, reused deliberately to isolate the dialect-selection variable.
IP uses TEST-NET-1 192.0.2.44; user/site identifiers are clearly synthetic fixture strings; asset/click/tracking URLs use reserved .test hostnames.
provenance.sanitized: No real visitor, publisher or advertiser data. IP 192.0.2.44 is TEST-NET-1; user.id/site.id are synthetic-fixture strings; every asset/click/tracking URL uses a reserved .test hostname.

ext.title: A quiet harbor at dawn
ext.description: Compare three original travel-planning tools before you book.

specNotes: packages/core/dialects/iab.js has no claimsBid predicate, so rules-response.js's base IAB rule (a bid with neither a string adm nor a string nurl draws response.bid.payload_missing, WARNING) fires unconditionally — this is documented, correct behaviour for the default dialect, not a defect.

Because the default dialect never inspects bid.ext at all, none of the inpage-push.* field checks (title/image/click required, icon/description/cta length limits) run either — the bid's well-formed ext content is simply unexamined under this dialect, which is the contract this case pins.

OpenRTB object-model requirements require at least one Banner, Video, Audio or Native object. A widget/zone extension alone does not satisfy that baseline requirement; imp.format_required is an expected error under both the IAB baseline and the current response-focused inpage-push dialect. The vendor format-tag/preview gap is separate from this correct diagnostic.
notes: Same bid.ext bytes as inpage-x-widget-openrtb-canonical, deliberately reused so the only variable between the two cases is case.dialect.

preview.limitation: No renderable creative field (adm/native/iurl) is present in the response; the winning bid's content lives entirely in bid.ext, which the preview pipeline never reads regardless of the selected dialect.
preview.capabilityGap: Dialect selection is a Core validation concept only; the front-end creative preview does not consult it at all, so this bid renders exactly as empty under 'iab' as it would under 'inpage-push'.

knownGap.note: 028: Core and HTTP expectations pass. Retained signatures describe unresolved preview behavior owned by Opus; no preview expectation was changed.
